destinations.name: New York
destinations.summary: A gift from France, raising a torch over New York Harbor.
destinations.story: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from the people of France, dedicated in 1886 on Liberty Island. Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi designed the sculpture, and Gustave Eiffel's company engineered its internal framework. Her copper skin has weathered to green, and ferries carry visitors across the harbor.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the Statue of Liberty with raised torch above the harbor at golden hour.

destinations.name: San Francisco
destinations.summary: An orange suspension bridge across the Golden Gate strait, often wrapped in fog.
destinations.story: The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937, linking San Francisco to Marin County across the mouth of San Francisco Bay. Its main span was the longest of any suspension bridge in the world until 1964. The distinctive International Orange paint helps it stand out in the frequent fog.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the red-orange Golden Gate Bridge with fog drifting through its towers at sunset.

destinations.name: Grand Canyon
destinations.summary: A mile-deep gorge carved by the Colorado River.
destinations.story: The Grand Canyon in Arizona is about 277 miles long and more than a mile deep, carved over millions of years by the Colorado River. Layers of rock exposed in its walls record a long geological history, and Grand Canyon National Park draws visitors to its rim viewpoints and trails.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of stepped red canyon walls with the Colorado River far below and a condor in the sky.

destinations.name: Lake Louise
destinations.summary: A turquoise glacial lake beneath the peaks of the Canadian Rockies.
destinations.story: Lake Louise lies in Banff National Park, Canada's oldest national park, within a Rocky Mountains UNESCO World Heritage Site. Rock flour carried by glacial meltwater gives the lake its striking turquoise colour in summer, and in winter it freezes over.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a snow-capped peak mirrored in a still lake with red canoes and pine trees.

destinations.name: Chichén Itzá
destinations.summary: A Maya city dominated by the stepped pyramid of El Castillo.
destinations.story: Chichén Itzá was a major city of the Maya civilization on the Yucatán Peninsula. Its pyramid El Castillo has four staircases of 91 steps each, and around the equinoxes the afternoon light and shadow can suggest a serpent descending the north stairway. The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the stepped pyramid of El Castillo among jungle trees and palms.

destinations.name: Yellowstone
destinations.summary: A geyser that erupts on a famously regular schedule.
destinations.story: Old Faithful in Yellowstone National Park, the world's first national park, erupts about every 90 minutes on average. Rangers publish predicted eruption times, and visitors gather on the boardwalk to watch columns of steam and hot water rise above the pines.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a column of steam erupting from a geyser among pine trees with visitors on a boardwalk.

destinations.name: Niagara Falls
destinations.summary: Three waterfalls on the Niagara River between Canada and the United States.
destinations.story: Niagara Falls consists of the Horseshoe Falls, the American Falls and the smaller Bridal Veil Falls, on the border between Ontario and New York. Boat tours carry visitors into the mist at the base of the falls.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the curved crest of Niagara's Horseshoe Falls with rising mist and a tour boat.

destinations.name: New Orleans
destinations.summary: Iron-balconied streets, live jazz and Creole cooking.
destinations.story: The French Quarter is the oldest neighbourhood in New Orleans, laid out in the early 18th century. Its streets are lined with Creole townhouses and cast-iron balconies, and live jazz and Creole and Cajun cooking are part of everyday life here.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of colourful townhouses with wrought-iron balconies and a gas lamp.

destinations.name: Honolulu
destinations.summary: A volcanic crater overlooking Waikiki Beach.
destinations.story: Diamond Head, known in Hawaiian as Lēʻahi, is a volcanic tuff cone on the island of Oʻahu. A trail leads from the crater floor to the summit, where views stretch along Waikiki and the Pacific coast.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the Diamond Head crater ridge above a sandy beach framed by two palm trees.
